title: Primary Function
learningObjectives: Identify the coupling's primary mechanical role.
student: State the primary mechanical function of the flanged coupling.
instructor: The coupling joins two coaxial shafts and transfers torque from the driving shaft to the driven shaft while maintaining rotational continuity.

title: External Loading
student: Identify the external loading represented in the simplified model.
instructor: Equal and opposite torques of magnitude T act on the two shafts, representing driver input and driven-machine resistance.

title: Torque Load Path
student: Trace the torque load path from the driving machine to the driven machine.
instructor: The path is driving shaft, first flange, bolt group in shear, second flange, driven shaft, and driven machine.

title: Compared Mechanical Responses
learningObjectives: Identify the two stresses compared by the design criterion.
student: Identify the two mechanical responses compared in this problem.
instructor: The design compares maximum torsional shear stress at the shaft surface with average direct shear stress in each coupling bolt.

title: Relevant Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify variables governing shaft and bolt stress.
student: Identify the geometric and loading variables that govern the two stresses.
instructor: The variables are torque T, shaft radius r, bolt-circle radius R, bolt diameter db, and bolt count n.

title: Load-Sharing Interpretation
student: Under the base idealization, why does each bolt carry the same tangential force?
instructor: The bolts are identical, equally spaced at the same radius, and connected by rigid flanges, so symmetry gives equal tangential force in every bolt.

title: Scope of the Base Problem
learningObjectives: Distinguish the base comparison from full coupling design.
student: Identify important real coupling behaviors excluded from the base model.
instructor: The model excludes preload and frictional torque transfer, bolt bearing, flange flexure, shaft bending, fatigue, fit, alignment, and local stress concentrations.

title: Student-Generated Coupling Idealization
learningObjectives: Create a coupling model before viewing the reference figure.
student: Before using the reference figure, draw two coaxial shafts, mating rigid flanges, n equally spaced bolts at radius R, shaft radius r, bolt diameter db, and applied torques.
instructor: A valid model preserves the coaxial shafts, circular bolt pattern, equal torque magnitude on each side, and all symbolic dimensions needed for shaft and bolt stress.
gradingNotes: A clear 2D or isometric model is acceptable.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State assumptions supporting uniform bolt-group analysis.
student: State the assumptions used in the base mechanics model.
instructor: Assume solid circular shafts, rigid flanges, identical equally spaced bolts, uniform tangential bolt force, single direct-shear area per bolt, static torque, and neglected preload friction, bending, bearing, fatigue, and stress concentration.

title: Analysis Plan
learningObjectives: Plan the symbolic and numerical design sequence.
student: List the calculation sequence needed to determine and verify the bolt count.
instructor: Derive shaft stress; write bolt-group torque equilibrium; derive bolt stress; equate the two stresses; solve for theoretical n; round upward to an allowed pattern; and verify the selected bolt stress.

title: Boundary Conditions and Torque Equilibrium
student: Describe the boundary/load representation and write the global torque-equilibrium condition.
instructor: The machine sides apply equal and opposite torques. For steady transmission, the shaft and coupling carry constant internal torque magnitude {{coupling_torque_Nmm}} N·mm.

title: Maximum Shaft Shear Stress
learningObjectives: Derive and evaluate maximum shaft shear stress.
student: Derive the maximum torsional shear stress in the solid shaft and evaluate it for the assigned values.

title: Tangential Force in Each Bolt
learningObjectives: Relate total torque to individual bolt force.
student: Assuming uniform load sharing among n bolts at radius R, determine the tangential force carried by each bolt.
instructor: Torque equilibrium gives T = nFbR, so Fb = T/(nR). For the selected pattern, Fb = {{coupling_bolt_force_N}} N.

title: Average Shear Stress in Each Bolt
student: Derive the average direct shear stress in each bolt.

title: Required Theoretical Bolt Count
learningObjectives: Derive the symbolic minimum bolt count.
student: Set average bolt shear stress equal to maximum shaft shear stress and solve for theoretical bolt count.
instructor: Equating 4T/(nπR db2) and 2T/(πr3) gives nreq = 2r3/(R db2) = {{coupling_n_req}}. Torque and π cancel because both stresses scale linearly with torque.

title: Practical Integer Selection
learningObjectives: Convert theoretical count into an allowed bolt pattern.
student: Select the smallest allowed bolt pattern not less than the theoretical requirement.
instructor: The smallest unrestricted integer is {{coupling_n_integer}} bolts. Applying the assigned pattern increment gives {{coupling_n_selected}} bolts. {{coupling_pattern_assessment}}

title: Selected-Pattern Verification
learningObjectives: Verify the selected bolt pattern against the criterion.
student: Calculate bolt force and bolt shear stress for the selected pattern, then verify the stress inequality.
instructor: Each selected bolt carries {{coupling_bolt_force_N}} N, producing τb = {{coupling_bolt_tau_MPa}} MPa. The ratio τb/τshaft,max is {{coupling_stress_ratio}}. {{coupling_stress_assessment}}

title: Sensitivity and Design Modification
learningObjectives: Interpret parameter sensitivity from the symbolic result.
student: Explain how changing r, R, or db affects required bolt count.
instructor: The requirement scales as n proportional to r3, 1/R, and 1/db2. Increasing bolt-circle radius or bolt diameter reduces required count, while increasing shaft radius raises it strongly under this stress-matching criterion.

title: Engineering Assessment
student: Provide a concise mechanics-based recommendation for the bolt pattern and identify omitted design checks.
instructor:
{{coupling_recommendation}}

A complete design must also check bolt bearing and fatigue, flange strength and flexure, preload and friction, shaft-hub details, fit, alignment, stress concentrations, and applicable coupling standards.
gradingNotes: The recommendation must be limited to the stated stress-matching model.
